title: Maximum Array Hopping Score I
statement:
You stand at index `0` of the integer array `nums` and want to reach its last index, `nums.length - 1`. In one hop you move from your current index `i` to any later index `j` (`j > i`), and that hop earns `(j - i) * nums[j]` points.

Return the largest total number of points you can collect over a sequence of hops that ends at the last index.
notes:
## Intuition

A route is a chain of hops `0 = i0 < i1 < ... < ik = n - 1`, and trying every chain is exponential. But the best way to land on index `j` only depends on where the last hop starts: it is the best way to land on some earlier `i`, plus `(j - i) * nums[j]` for the final hop. That is a one-dimensional DP over landing indices. (A sharper observation, needed for the larger version of this problem, is that each unit of distance is paid at the value you land on, so always jumping to the largest value ahead is optimal and gives O(n). With at most 1000 elements the quadratic DP is plenty.)

## Approach

1. `dp[j]` is the best score of a route from index `0` that ends exactly at `j`; `dp[0] = 0`.
2. For each `j` from `1` to `n - 1`, try every index `i < j` as the start of the last hop: `dp[i] + (j - i) * nums[j]`.
3. Keep the largest candidate in `dp[j]`.
4. Return `dp[n - 1]`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 5, 8]`, `dp = [0, 0, 0]`.

- `j = 1`: from `i = 0` the hop earns `1 * 5 = 5`, so `dp[1] = 5`.
- `j = 2`: from `i = 0` the route earns `0 + 2 * 8 = 16`; from `i = 1` it earns `5 + 1 * 8 = 13`. So `dp[2] = 16`.

The answer is `dp[2] = 16`: one long hop onto the `8`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): every pair `i < j` is tried once.
- Space: O(n) for `dp`.

## Pitfalls

- A hop is paid with the value where it **lands**, `nums[j]`, not where it starts.
- Hopping straight to the end is not always best: in example 2 it earns `6 * 3 = 18`, while landing on the `9` first earns `42`.
- Jumping to the *next* larger value is not the right greedy either; on `[1, 5, 8]` it lands on `5` and scores `13` instead of `16`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `nums` |
| `dp[j]` | best score of a route that ends at index `j` |
| `j` | the landing index being computed |
| `i` | where the last hop into `j` starts |

narration.2: n is the number of positions; every route must end at index n - 1.
narration.3: dp[j] will hold the best score of a route ending at index j; dp[0] stays 0 because the route starts there.
narration.5: Fill in the landing indices from left to right, so every earlier dp value is final.
narration.6: Try every earlier index i as the start of the last hop into j.
narration.7: Best score up to i plus the final hop's (j - i) * nums[j]; keep the larger value.
narration.10: The best route that ends at the last index is the answer.
